payload.headline: Alphabet slips 1.08% to 279.05 above support; hold, add only at 234.35

summary.thesis: Sales are growing faster and the balance sheet is strong, but free cash flow fell from 73.6B to 19.7B and earnings estimates are dropping, so the stock is not cheap at 279.05.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only at 234.35. Swing: wait for a better setup.
summary.act_at: add at 234.35; swing entry only on a daily close above 300.07

payload.happening: Alphabet closed at 279.05, down 1.08% on the day. It sits just above the 271.77–277.07 support zone and below its falling 20-day average of 285.64. A new 8-K filing ('Other events') was confirmed, but its contents are not in our data. Kagi, a Google alternative, reportedly launched an email service. The next earnings report is on 2027-02-03.
payload.business: Things that change the business: sales growth sped up to 24.65% year over year, from 21.79% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 33.32% from 32.19%. Cash is the weak spot. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after investment, fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, which is only 4.19% of sales. The filings show that each dollar invested now earns 24¢ a year, down from 40¢ three years ago, so the heavy spending is not paying back yet. Reported profit is boosted by one-off gains: the net margin of 50.03% is above the operating margin of 33.32%. That is also why analysts expect next-year EPS of 14.97, below this year's 19.56. Nothing here puts the company's survival at risk. Net cash is 139.0B and liquidity is 265.1B. What is at risk is the price, which assumes about 36% growth a year against the 17% a year delivered over three years. Things that change only sentiment or governance: the reported Kagi launch is a small competitive headline. The 8-K contents are unknown, so we draw no conclusion from it. The wider tech market is in a downtrend, which weighs on sentiment.

worth.text: The methods disagree a lot. A cash-flow model (DCF, which values the company on its future cash) built on today's 19.7B of free cash flow gives 26 / 51.55 / 70.45 per share (bear / base / bull). Even if that cash grew 30% a year at the start, the value would only be 79.7. On the stock's own history of price-to-sales (the price compared with one year of sales), the range is 234.35 / 282.1 / 375.22. The stock now trades at 7.3 times sales, against a peer median of 4.8, and sits at the 50th percentile of its own 5-year range. On earnings it looks cheap at 14.6 times trailing earnings. But 18.6 times next year's earnings is a fairer picture, because this year's profit includes one-off gains. The gap between the methods comes from one input: free cash flow. At 19.7B, the stock looks very expensive. If cash flow gets back toward its earlier 73.6B, the price-to-sales history becomes the better guide. Our fair-value range is 234.35 to 282.1, so 279.05 sits near the top of it.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the earlier 73.6B as the spending pays off; if it stays near 19.7B, even 234.35 is generous.

bull: Sales growth sped up to 24.65% year over year, from 21.79% two quarters ago.
Operating margin rose to 33.32% from 32.19%, so growth is not coming at the cost of profitability.
Net cash of 139.0B and liquidity of 265.1B can carry a long spending cycle.
bear: Trailing free cash flow fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, a free cash flow margin of only 4.19%.
Analysts cut this year's EPS estimate by 5.2% in 30 days to 19.56, and next year's EPS estimate of 14.97 is lower still.
The price implies about 36% growth a year against 17% delivered over three years, and the stock trades at 7.3 times sales against a peer median of 4.8.

levels.what: Today's close, near the top of the 234.35–282.1 fair range. That leaves no room for error, so no new buying here.
Bottom of the support zone. A close below it would end the current range and open the way toward lower levels.
Low end of the own-history range and the add level. It allows for free cash flow staying weak for a while.

longterm.why: Faster sales and a strong balance sheet support holding, but weak cash flow and falling estimates do not justify paying near the top of fair value. Add only at 234.35.

swing.why: A stop below 271.77 is less than one normal day's move (average true range, or ATR, of 11.5) from 279.05, and the first ceiling at 293.72–300.07 caps the upside. Enter only on a daily close above 300.07 with 304.97 as the next target, or on a pullback that holds the 271.77–277.07 zone.

decision.timing: The next report is on 2027-02-03, outside the December options window. December options imply a move of about 8.2% by 2026-12-18 (down from 10.2% yesterday). February options, which include the report, imply 15.1%, so the long-term add at 234.35 can wait for the report's cash-flow numbers.

change_mind: A daily close above 300.07, where the largest call open interest sits at the 300 strike (29377 contracts), would turn the swing call to enter, with 304.97–311.03 as the target zone.
A daily close below 271.77 would break support; the long-term plan would then be to add only at 234.35, not before.

If the 2027-02-03 report shows trailing free cash flow moving back above 19.7B toward 73.6B, the fair range would shift toward the own-history mid of 282.1 and above. A further cut to this year's EPS estimate below 19.56 would point the other way.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold and add only at 234.35; the close of 279.05 stayed above the 271.77–277.07 support while estimates kept falling (this year's EPS down 5.2% in 30 days), which confirms there is no reason to buy more or to sell.
